name: Sacred Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada)
wiki: Relic of the tooth of the Buddha
summary: The left canine tooth of the Buddha, brought from Kalinga in the 4th century. Whoever held it held the right to rule, so it moved with the capital for fifteen centuries.
historiography: The Portuguese claimed to have captured the tooth at Jaffna in 1560 and burned it in Goa in 1561. Sinhala tradition answers that the relic taken was a replica, or that the real one was already hidden at Delgamuwa. Some stations rest only on later tradition.

stations.label: c. 310 CE
stations.note: Landed, in tradition, by Hemamala and Danta.

stations.label: c. 310-1017
stations.note: Kept in the Dhammacakka house by the palace; Faxian saw its annual procession c. 410.
Taken south to Ruhuna, beyond Chola control (region; exact place unknown).
Housed by Vijayabahu I in the Atadage, later in Nissanka Malla's Hatadage, at Polonnaruwa.

stations.label: c. 1215-1220
stations.note: Hidden in the Kotmale hills during Magha's rule.

name: Sacred Bowl Relic (Patra Dhatu)
summary: The Buddha's alms bowl, said by the chronicle to have been sent by Asoka, was kept in the royal palace. It travelled with the Tooth Relic as a second palladium until it disappears from the record in the Kotte period.
historiography: Its fate after the 15th-16th century is unknown.

name: Sri Maha Bodhi and its saplings
summary: A branch of the Bodhi tree of Bodh Gaya, the most venerated object of use (paribhogika) relic. The Mahavamsa names the places where the first eight saplings were planted. Tradition later counts 32 saplings across the island.

name: The Sacred Footprint (Sri Pada)
summary: The footprint on Samanalakanda is venerated by four religions. Buddhists hold it to be the Buddha's, impressed on his third visit.
